title: Littlewood Polynomial
content: A polynomial with all coefficients in {-1, +1}. Named after J.E. Littlewood who studied their extremal properties on the unit circle. More restrictive than unimodular (|aᵢ|=1).

title: Erdős #1150 Conjecture
content: There exists universal c > 0 such that every degree-n Littlewood polynomial has max_{|z|=1}|P(z)| > (1+c)√n for large n. Equivalently, ultraflat Littlewood polynomials do not exist.

title: Parseval Lower Bound
content: From Parseval's identity: ∫|P(e^{iθ})|² dθ/2π = Σ|aᵢ|² = n+1. Since max|P|² ≥ average|P|², we get max|P| ≥ √(n+1). This is sharp in the limit for unimodular coefficients (Kahane) but NOT for ±1.

title: BBMST Flat Polynomials (2019)
content: Balister-Bollobás-Morris-Sahasrabudhe-Tiba proved flat Littlewood polynomials exist: c₁√n ≤ |P(z)| ≤ c₂√n on |z|=1. This resolved Erdős #228 but does NOT resolve #1150, since flat (bounded ratio) is weaker than ultraflat (ratio → 1).

title: Kahane's Unimodular Ultraflat (1980)
content: For general unimodular coefficients (|aᵢ|=1), Kahane proved ultraflat polynomials exist: |P(z)| = (1+o(1))√n uniformly on |z|=1. The restriction to ±1 coefficients makes this dramatically harder. The discreteness of {-1,+1} is the essential obstruction.
